title: The Limits of Predicting Creativity
source: AI-generated original passage. IELTS-style practice; no published test text reproduced.
passageHtml:
A Creativity is often treated as a quality that organisations urgently need but struggle to identify. Employers ask for creative applicants, schools promise to develop creative learners, and governments praise creative industries. Yet prediction remains difficult. A person who produces an original idea in one setting may repeat familiar patterns in another. Creativity is not a single substance that can be measured like height or temperature.

B Traditional tests of creativity have often asked participants to generate many uses for an ordinary object, such as a brick or a paperclip. Responses are scored for fluency, originality and flexibility. These tasks are attractive because they are simple to administer and compare. However, they may reward speed and verbal confidence more than deep creative work. A quiet participant who develops one unusual solution slowly may appear less creative than someone who lists many obvious ideas quickly.

C Biographical indicators are also tempting. Some selection systems look for earlier achievements in art, science or entrepreneurship. Past achievement can be meaningful, but it is also shaped by opportunity. A student with access to mentors, materials and time may build an impressive portfolio, while another with equal potential may have had little chance to demonstrate it. Predicting future creativity from past products can therefore reproduce existing inequalities.

D Domain knowledge complicates the picture further. Popular accounts sometimes describe creativity as freedom from rules, but many innovations come from deep familiarity with a field. A jazz musician, for example, can improvise because she knows conventions well enough to bend them. At the same time, expertise can create habits that make alternatives harder to see. Knowledge is therefore both a resource and a constraint.

E Collaboration adds another difficulty. Creative outcomes are often credited to individuals, yet ideas may emerge through conversation, criticism and revision. In a design studio or laboratory, the final product may depend on people who asked useful questions as much as on the person who proposed the first idea. A test that isolates individuals may miss the social process by which creativity develops.

F Digital tools now promise to identify creative potential through data: patterns of search, editing histories, social networks or even eye movements. Such measures may reveal useful clues, but they risk confusing activity with insight. A person who revises a document many times is not necessarily more creative than one who changes it rarely. The trace left by work is not the same as the quality of thought behind it.

G This does not mean that creativity cannot be supported or assessed at all. It means that prediction should be modest. The most useful assessments combine evidence from different contexts and ask what conditions allow a person to produce original and valuable work. Instead of searching for a permanent creative type, institutions may do better to design environments in which more people can act creatively.

questions.question: What is the main problem introduced in Paragraph A?
options: Creativity is no longer valued by employers.
Creativity is difficult to predict reliably.
Original ideas are easy to measure.
questions.answer: Creativity is difficult to predict reliably.
questions.reason_ja: A段落では、組織や学校が creativity を求めている一方で、prediction remains difficult と述べています。つまり、創造性を信頼性高く予測することが難しいという問題提起です。

questions.question: Traditional creativity tests may favour people who produce many quick verbal responses.
questions.evidence: they may reward speed and verbal confidence more than deep creative work.
questions.reason_ja: B段落では、従来型テストが deep creative work よりも speed and verbal confidence を評価してしまう可能性があると述べています。many quick verbal responses はこの内容の言い換えです。

questions.question: A person who gives only one answer can never be highly creative.
questions.evidence: A quiet participant who develops one unusual solution slowly may appear less creative...
questions.reason_ja: 本文Bは、ゆっくり一つの unusual solution を考える参加者が、見かけ上は低く評価される可能性を述べています。これは実際に創造性がないという意味ではありません。can never という断定が本文と矛盾します。

questions.question: Past achievements always provide a fair indication of future creative potential.
questions.evidence: Past achievement can be meaningful, but it is also shaped by opportunity.
questions.reason_ja: C段落では、過去の実績は意味を持つ場合もあるが、機会の差によって形作られると述べています。したがって、それが常に公平な指標になるわけではありません。always が本文と矛盾します。

questions.question: The passage states that portfolios are required for all science courses.
questions.evidence: A student with access to mentors, materials and time may build an impressive portfolio...
questions.reason_ja: portfolio は実績の例として登場するだけです。「すべての科学コースで必要」という情報は本文中にないため NOT GIVEN です。
questions.not_given_reason: 本文は portfolio を過去の実績の例として挙げていますが、科学コースで全員に必要だとは述べていません。

questions.question: Expert knowledge can both help and limit creativity.
questions.evidence: Knowledge is therefore both a resource and a constraint.
questions.reason_ja: D段落の結論で、Knowledge is therefore both a resource and a constraint. と述べています。resource は助けになるもの、constraint は制約です。したがって TRUE です。

questions.question: Creative work is always best assessed by testing individuals separately.
questions.evidence: A test that isolates individuals may miss the social process by which creativity develops.
questions.reason_ja: E段落では、個人を切り離したテストは、創造性が発展する social process を見落とす可能性があると述べています。always best assessed という断定は本文と反対です。

questions.question: Complete the summary. Write ONE WORD ONLY from the passage for each answer.
questions.summaryHtml: Creativity tests that count many responses may overvalue speed rather than deep work. Earlier achievement is influenced by {{34|Q34}}, so it may reproduce {{35|Q35}}. In specialist fields, knowledge can be both a resource and a {{36|Q36}}. Digital traces may show activity, but not necessarily {{37|Q37}}.

evidence.34: it is also shaped by opportunity
evidence.36: Knowledge is therefore both a resource and a constraint.

reason_ja.34: 本文Cの shaped by opportunity に対応します。過去の実績は本人の力だけでなく、機会の有無に左右されます。
reason_ja.35: その結果として existing inequalities を reproduce する可能性があると本文にあります。ONE WORD ONLY なので inequalities が答えです。
reason_ja.36: 本文Dの結論文そのままです。知識は resource であると同時に constraint でもあります。
reason_ja.37: F段落では、デジタル指標が activity と insight を混同する危険があると述べています。trace は活動の跡であり、思考の質そのものではありません。

questions.question: Which paragraph questions the fairness of using earlier accomplishments to predict creativity?
questions.evidence: Predicting future creativity from past products can therefore reproduce existing inequalities.
questions.reason_ja: C段落では、過去の実績が機会の差に左右され、将来の創造性予測に使うと不平等を再生産する可能性があると述べています。fairness of using earlier accomplishments がこの内容に対応します。

questions.question: Which paragraph argues that creative products may depend on interaction among several people?
questions.evidence: ideas may emerge through conversation, criticism and revision.
keyword_pairs: may depend on people who asked useful questions
questions.reason_ja: E段落では、創造的な成果が個人だけでなく、会話、批判、修正を通して生まれると説明しています。interaction among several people はこの social process の言い換えです。

questions.question: The best title for this passage is...
options: Why Creativity Should Not Be Taught
How Digital Data Solves Creativity Testing
questions.reason_ja: 本文全体は、創造性が重要である一方、従来テスト、過去の実績、専門知識、協働、デジタルデータのいずれにも予測上の限界があるという流れです。最終段落でも prediction should be modest と述べています。したがって、最も本文全体を表すタイトルは The Limits of Predicting Creativity です。
